title: Strange type behavior when an abstract function that should return an int returns a float
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible only when exporting, but NOT in the editor: 4.7.1, 4.7
- Reproducible in editor and when exporting: 4.6.3 and below(?)

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.93 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When a script extends an abstract class and implements a function that is expected to return a float returns an integer, the resulting value becomes some sort of float+int combination that behaves strangely. For example, it may output that `3.5 * .8` is `4613487458278336103`. 
This strange combination also affects other variables that already have types. For example, an existing float could be multiplied by this combination and become an int instead.

### Steps to reproduce

Use the MRP below. If you're testing on 4.7 or later, you'll need to first export the project in debug mode, and run the console version. 
If you're on 4.6.3 or earlier, simply run the project from your editor.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30381269/bug.zip)
